references.text: Jesus' opponents accuse him of having a demon, which directly mirrors their earlier accusation that he is a Samaritan and possessed, confirming that they view him as an enemy of the truth.
Here the crowd also accuses Jesus of having a demon, a repetition of the same kind of denial and hostility expressed in John 8:48.
A new group of Jews repeats the accusation that Jesus is possessed by a demon, showing consistent resistance to his message throughout the gospel.

The Pharisees split into two groups, with one claiming that Jesus is not from God because he breaks the Sabbath, while the other asks how a sinner can perform such signs, reflecting the same doubt and accusation of demonic influence.
